bug_description.normalized: A single attacker-controlled `lxc.rootfs.options` define that contains an overlong `idmap=` substring makes `parse_lxc_mntopts()` pass the substring span to `strlcpy()` as the destination size. `strlcpy()` then copies 5676 bytes into `rootfs->mnt_opts.userns_path[PATH_MAX]` and overflows the heap-allocated `lxc_conf` object before the subsequent length check runs.

source.code: *dot = '\0'; value = dot + 1; ... new->key = move_ptr(k); new->val = move_ptr(v);
source.description: First project-side parse/materialization of the attacker buffer: `parse_new_conf_line()` splits the single input line at the first `=` and stores a `new_config_item` whose key is `lxc.rootfs.options` and whose value is the long attacker-controlled options string later searched for `idmap=`.
source.value_from: The libFuzzer harness in `src/tests/fuzz-lxc-define-load.c` copies the staged 5714-byte PoC into NUL-terminated `new_str` and passes it to `lxc_config_define_add(&defines, new_str)`. The witness is a single config define beginning `lxc.rootfs.options=`; its parsed value contains `idmap=` at offset 11 and 5676 non-comma bytes before the next comma (sha256 `7834efbe3c8731789ff3d9f782afe4cb525cc54505d50963bb7b41e6dc18557d`).

tainted_value_origin.description: The parsed `new->val` string is the first vulnerability-relevant project value. It preserves the attacker-controlled `lxc.rootfs.options` payload, including the embedded `idmap=` substring later treated as an LXC-specific mount option.

sink.description: ASan crash site. `strlcpy()` interprets the caller-supplied 5677 as destination capacity, computes a 5676-byte copy, and writes past `rootfs->mnt_opts.userns_path` inside the heap `lxc_conf` allocation.
sink.note: The sanitizer trace reports `WRITE of size 5676` at this `memcpy` and the allocation stack points to `lxc_conf_init()`.

root_cause.description: The caller computes the distance from `p2` to the next comma and passes that attacker-derived span as `strlcpy()`'s `size` argument, even though the destination is `opts->userns_path[PATH_MAX]`; the bounds check only executes after the call returns.
root_cause.note: In the witnessed PoC, `idmap_path - p2 + 1` is 5677 while `sizeof(opts->userns_path)` is 4096.

parser_admitted.description: The staged witness is admitted as an `lxc.` config define when `parse_new_conf_line()` finds the first `=` and constructs a `new_config_item` for `lxc.rootfs.options`.

coarse_trace.summary: Parse the single attacker-controlled config string into `new_item->key = "lxc.rootfs.options"` and the long `new_item->val` options payload.
Dispatch the parsed key/value pair through the config table, routing `lxc.rootfs.options` to `set_config_rootfs_options()`.
Duplicate the attacker-controlled options string and pass it with `rootfs->mnt_opts` into `parse_lxc_mntopts()`.
Find the embedded `idmap=` substring, derive the copy span from the next comma, and pass that span to `strlcpy()` as if it were destination capacity.
Use the oversized caller-supplied size to copy 5676 bytes into the 4096-byte `userns_path`, producing the ASan-observed heap-buffer-overflow.

fine_trace.code: *dot = '\0'; value = dot + 1; ... new->key = move_ptr(k); new->val = move_ptr(v);
fine_trace.note: The parser accepts the single NUL-terminated attacker string as an `lxc.` config define, splits at the first `=`, and stores `new->key = "lxc.rootfs.options"` with a 5695-byte `new->val` whose contents still include `idmap=` at offset 11.

fine_trace.code: config = lxc_get_config(key); ret = config->set(key, v, conf, NULL);
fine_trace.note: Applying the parsed define dispatches the attacker-controlled value through the config table; the `lxc.rootfs.options` entry selects `set_config_rootfs_options()` as the setter.

The setter duplicates the attacker-controlled options string into mutable `dup` and passes it with `rootfs->mnt_opts` to `parse_lxc_mntopts()`. `rootfs->mnt_opts.userns_path` is the fixed 4096-byte destination array inside the heap `lxc_conf` object allocated by `lxc_conf_init()`.

fine_trace.code: p = strstr(mnt_opts, opt_name); ... p2 = p; p2 += STRLITERALLEN("idmap=");
fine_trace.note: On the `LXC_MOUNT_IDMAP` iteration (`opt_name == "idmap="`), `strstr()` finds the embedded `idmap=` substring inside `dup` and advances `p2` to the first byte after `idmap=`. `p2` becomes the start of the would-be path string.
The next comma after `p2` is 5676 bytes later in the witness, so the size expression used by the next statement, `idmap_path - p2 + 1`, evaluates to 5677.

The code passes that 5677-byte source span to `strlcpy()` as if it were the destination capacity. Since `opts->userns_path` is only `PATH_MAX` (4096) bytes, this call is already unsafe before any check runs.

fine_trace.code: size_t len = (ret >= size) ? size - 1 : ret; memcpy(dest, src, len); dest[len] = '\0';
fine_trace.note: Inside `strlcpy()`, `ret = strlen(src)` is 5678 and caller-supplied `size` is 5677, so `len` becomes 5676. `memcpy(dest, src, len)` writes 5676 bytes into the 4096-byte `userns_path`, then `dest[len] = '\0'` writes one byte farther; ASan reports the overflow at the `memcpy` line.
The only bounds check runs after `strlcpy()` returns the source length, so it can only report the excessive path after step 7 has already overwritten the heap object.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run executed `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_33556 run --version vulnerable --expect crash`, which fed `poc` to `/out/fuzz-lxc-define-load` and reproduced `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow WRITE` in `strlcpy` with stack `parse_lxc_mntopts -> set_config_rootfs_options`.

format.name: Single NUL-terminated LXC config define consumed by `fuzz-lxc-define-load`
format.contract: The staged witness is one NUL-free config string beginning `lxc.rootfs.options=`. Its parsed value must preserve an embedded `idmap=` substring and keep at least 4096 non-comma bytes between the first byte after `idmap=` and the next comma or end of string, so `parse_lxc_mntopts()` derives `idmap_path - p2 + 1 > sizeof(opts->userns_path)` and still reaches the vulnerable `strlcpy()` call. This contract is limited to the witnessed single-line define path and not all malformed LXC configuration inputs.
